title: Shadow traffic failover playbook and SLO realignment
summary: Follow-up after intermittent degradations during peak weekend. Reviewed shadow traffic run, failover behavior, SLO targets, and next steps for hardening the fallback path and automating canary promotion. Agreed on short-term mitigations and owner assignments; Redwood to deliver a pilot failover runbook and a tailored SLO proposal.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-27 16:30 UTC
Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Nina (Vantage Head of Platform), Carlos (Vantage SRE), Avery (Vantage CTO), Samir (Vantage Product)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining. we want to run through the weekend incident, what we saw in shadow traffic, and the concrete canary/failover plan. is the timing still ok?
00:10 Nina: yes fine, i'm on mobile but i have the logs open, thanks.
00:17 Liam: quick note first — i ran the shadow runbook last night with the extra logging flags, so we have a better view of prefix cache hit rates and eviction spikes. the results are in the deck link i shared in chat (link: https://redwood.ai/shadow-run-aug26).
00:31 Carlos: oh right that link, saw it. first question — during the 11pm spike we saw request latencies jump from ~60ms to 350ms, and many requests hit the fallback which is our older service. curious how the KV cache eviction maps to that.
00:47 Liam: yeah the correlation was pretty clear — eviction wave started when sequence lengths spiked and concurrent requests increased, the runtime's batching got less efficient and we lost the warm KV pages. 
00:59 Maya: to clarify for everyone, by fallback you mean the configured model fallback path to our v1 small model, correct? sometimes the transcript or the logs call that "legacy" or "vPrime" which is confusing.
01:12 Avery: yes v1 small is the fallback. the problem we have is that the failover was too slow and our downstream systems experienced a mix of responses. customers saw inconsistencies. that's the CX risk.
01:26 Jordan: and we also saw noisy retries from the client side which amplified load. some of those retries were due to 503s coming from an LB health check flapping.
01:39 Carlos: there's a note in the incident doc that our autoscaler wasn't triggering in time because the metric was token-rate rather than concurrency.
01:48 Liam: yep we flagged that. autoscale policy should consider active concurrency and sampling of token backlog not just token rate.
02:02 Maya: okay let's run the proposed immediate mitigations then: 1) a controlled canary promotion using shadow traffic, 2) tighten TTL on some prefixes to reduce contention, 3) short-term SLO relaxation for burst windows and explicit customer comms. Nina, do you agree?
02:18 Nina: i do, but we need specifics — what does "controlled canary" mean operationally, and who runs it?
02:26 Liam: operationally: route 5% of traffic to a canary pool with identical model versions but isolated GK hardware, run for 2 hours, monitor tail latency P99 and error-rate, then either promote the canary or roll it back. we also want to run a shadow run in parallel at 20% to ensure cache warms without affecting production.
02:45 Carlos: question — can we make the canary auto-promote if its P99 is below threshold for 30 minutes? or do we want manual signoff?
02:55 Maya: i recommend auto-promote with a manual guardrail: auto-promote can be enabled but requires an owner to acknowledge within 20 minutes, otherwise it rolls back. reduces human-in-the-loop time but prevents silent promotions.
03:12 Samir: uh — small nit, what thresholds are we using for P99? current SLO is 200ms but that seems tight given the model size.
03:21 Avery: agreed, 200ms feels aggressive for heavy bursts. we should realign SLOs to operational reality if costs to reach them are prohibitive.
03:30 Liam: proposal: keep P50 at 60ms, P95 at 150ms, set P99 to 300ms during burst windows (defined as top 2% of traffic hours). outside burst windows, P99 target stays 200ms. we'll provide a sliding window and rolling percentiles in telemetry.
03:48 Nina: ok that helps us with customer-facing commitments. can you also document the fallback semantics? we saw a partial mix of outputs from the fallback model and the primary model; clients couldn't easily reconcile.
03:58 Jordan: action item for that: we need consistent circuit-breaker signals and a response header that indicates model version and confidence so clients can reconcile.
04:10 Carlos: the logs sometimes show the header as model=unknown, maybe due to missing metadata in older proxy.
04:18 Liam: that's likely the proxy shim. we'll add a hard-coded header in the runtime path for failovers.
04:25 Maya: i want to surface a telemetry gap — we don't currently trace KV cache misses to request IDs at the scale we need; that's in the deck as "telemetry gap 2". if we can't link misses to requests we can't root-cause properly.
04:40 Nina: that was painful to debug last weekend. can you add request-id->kv-event linking as a priority?
04:46 Liam: yes, we'll prioritize an instrumented build that attaches kv-eviction events to request IDs for 7 days retention.
04:55 Maya: good. next area — backlog and throttling. when the fallback trips we saw client retries starving the warm pool. proposed short-term throttling of retries at the LB with exponential backoff guidance to clients.
05:10 Samir: we'll add guidance to our SDK to implement jittered backoff and idempotency keys for duplicate suppression.
05:22 Carlos: also need a circuit breaker threshold that's visible in the console and can be toggled per-route. can Redwood expose that?
05:30 Liam: yes, Redwood Console can expose per-route circuit breaker toggles; we'll prepare a template with recommended default thresholds.
05:39 Maya: ok, let's capture concrete next steps. Jordan, do you have the list?
05:44 Jordan: sure — i'll read them aloud then we'll add deadlines. 1) Redwood to provide a failover runbook draft and canary automation script. 2) Redwood SE to deliver instrumented runtime build with kv->request tracing. 3) Vantage to update client SDKs with backoff guidance. 4) Joint SLO proposal with burst windows. 5) Short-term TTL adjustments and a rollback plan.
06:10 Avery: timeline? we need this before the upcoming marketing sale weekend in 10 days.
06:16 Maya: ok, we'll prioritize. suggested timing: runbook and canary script in 48 hours, instrumented build in 96 hours, SLO proposal in 72 hours, SDK guidelines in 5 days.
06:28 Nina: that sounds reasonable. can we schedule an execution call for the canary run with ops on day 3?
06:34 Maya: yes i'll create the invite.
06:37 Carlos: small comment — can the canary pool be on a different region to test cross-region fallback? we had region-specific latency last time.
06:46 Liam: we recommend same region to avoid cross-region variables; but we can run a separate cross-region smoke test after local canary is successful.
06:56 Samir: any compliance/audit concerns with shadow traffic? we are anonymizing payloads but want a confirmation from Redwood on retention and redaction.
07:06 Jordan: Redwood can provide the data retention policy: shadow logs retained 14 days by default for pilots, redacted payloads only, and we'll provide an audit doc and SOC2 note. link: https://redwood.ai/compliance/shadow-retention.pdf
07:22 Nina: good. also can you include an SLA note about auto-promote behavior? we need to include that in the internal escalation playbook.
07:30 Maya: yes, we'll add an appendix defining auto-promote guardrails and escalation contacts.
07:36 Carlos: another thing — during the incident the downstream feature toggle system had stale flags which caused some routes to be mis-routed to older code paths. not sure if Redwood or our side should own that detection.
07:48 Liam: sounds like joint ownership. Redwood can emit a mismatch metric when route header version != runtime header version; Vantage can alert on that metric.
07:58 Maya: perfect. any blockers we haven't covered?
08:02 Avery: main blocker is time — we need runs before the sale weekend. also need a dry-run checklist and preflight steps.
08:12 Jordan: we'll deliver a preflight checklist as part of the runbook (traffic snapshot, curl-based smoke tests, clear rollback commands, contacts).
08:20 Maya: ok let's do a quick recap then recording of owners.
08:24 Jordan: recap: 1) Failover runbook and canary automation — owner: Maya (Redwood) — due 2026-08-29. 2) Instrumented runtime build (kv->request tracing) — owner: Liam (Redwood SE) — due 2026-08-31. 3) SLO realignment proposal (burst windows) — owner: Jordan (Redwood CSM) — due 2026-08-30. 4) SDK retry/backoff guidance — owner: Samir (Vantage Product) — due 2026-09-01. 5) Console circuit-breaker template — owner: Liam — due 2026-08-30. 6) Compliance note on shadow retention — owner: Jordan — due 2026-08-29.
08:56 Nina: thanks. we'll block calendar for the canary execution on 2026-08-30 morning.
09:03 Maya: great. i'll send a followup with links and a preflight checklist. thanks everyone.
09:10 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: some speaker labels may be approximated (e.g., Maya vs. Maya Chen) and a few technical terms were transcribed as similar-sounding words (e.g., "KV" sometimes rendered as "K-Vee").
